capabilities.name: Typed memory curation
capabilities.notes: llm_agent owns typed model execution; MemoryAgent is the bounded policy layer and LongTermMemoryService remains the persistence/lifecycle owner. The whole plan is deterministically validated before mutation, IDs must come from the tenant/user-scoped candidate set, background chat exit has no delete authority, and failures degrade to no mutation.

capabilities.name: File ingestion workflow
capabilities.notes: File lifecycle truth belongs in Files.

capabilities.name: Qdrant vector search/storage
capabilities.notes: Production retrieval uses named dense and lexical sparse Qdrant vectors with bounded deterministic client-side RRF. The independent arms run concurrently through one process-owned two-worker/two-permit executor because server fusion cannot return the required per-arm diagnostics or enforce the chunk-id tie-break contract. Both arms share tenant/review filters. File/document cleanup uses an exact filtered count followed by filter-native delete, never a client-materialized point-ID list. One reusable Qdrant client is closed during service shutdown. Dense-only mode remains supported explicitly; a legacy collection without the named sparse schema requires rebuild/reindex.

capabilities.name: Eval candidate depth separate from production K
capabilities.notes: Known merged in audited main snapshot; verify current source.

capabilities.name: Per-item retrieval diagnostics trace
capabilities.notes: Bounded ids/ranks/scores only, including dense/sparse/fused ranks and arm provenance when available; opt-in per eval item and never stores chunk text.

capabilities.name: Deterministic stage failure attribution
capabilities.notes: Classifies each eval/benchmark item from its own retrieval trace into index/retrieval/pass_two/ranking/context/completeness/generation/grounding/stale_labels/pipeline_error, or unclassified when evidence is insufficient. No LLM is used to guess a retrieval-stage failure. Benchmark phases inherit it through the shared eval aggregate.

capabilities.name: Chat answer surface and Developer Inspector
capabilities.notes: Default answer surface shows answer/sources/feedback/compact quality only; identifiers, prompts, evaluator payloads and per-node timings belong to the inspector. Unmeasured review scores must never render as 0%.

capabilities.name: Semantic long-term memory retrieval
capabilities.notes: LongTermMemoryService is the single owner of memory persistence, lifecycle and retrieval. Writes use bounded deterministic consolidation: exact and semantic duplicates are suppressed or reinforced, declared fact keys supersede prior values only within the same canonical scope, ambiguous similarity preserves both facts for later policy, and temporal validity keeps superseded facts explicitly historical. Current retrieval excludes deleted/superseded facts unless history or as-of semantics are requested. Manual authenticated creates are explicit user signals, preserve the RabbitMQ request context into the write audit, and return the existing canonical memory for an exact retry instead of creating a duplicate. Manual delete uses canonical reload semantics; user_insight remains AI/system-managed and read-only. Memory vectors come only from the embedding service RPC (action 'embed'); MongoDB is canonical and Qdrant is derived. MemoryReconciliationService performs tenant-scoped, bounded, resumable repair for missing/stale/orphan/duplicate vectors and tombstoned deletes, while retrieval.embedding_status records partial failures for idempotent retry.

capabilities.name: Memory service competing-consumer replica scaleout
capabilities.notes: MEMORY_REPLICAS defaults to 1 and may be raised for RabbitMQ competing-consumer scaleout. Memory correctness state is external in MongoDB/Qdrant, embedding and LLM work remain external RPC calls, prefetch and executor admission stay bounded per replica, and the service loads no model. CONC-10 measured 200 read-only RPCs at concurrency 32: 334.394 req/s with one replica versus 839.850 req/s with two, 109/111 deliveries, zero errors, and about 57.6 MiB RSS per replica. This is a measured read-path result, not a claim of linear scaling for downstream-bound semantic writes or unlimited replicas.
